prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place named in the Song of Solomon, from Engedi to Lebanon, or Pharaoh's chariots (not Tirzah or Kedar)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place named in the Song of Solomon: Lebanon and the tops of Amana, Shenir and Hermon, the tower of Lebanon toward Damascus, Engedi, Carmel and Sharon, Heshbon and Gilead, or Pharaoh's chariots (Tirzah and the tents of Kedar are left out: their sites are not fixed in Church sources)
prompts.note: Mount Hermon (Shenir) sits on the Lebanon-Syria border, so both count. Jerusalem is scored as Israel.
prompts.summary: The Song of Solomon draws its imagery from the whole land: the vineyards of Engedi, the rose of Sharon, the cedars of Lebanon, the heights of Hermon, the pools of Heshbon and the goats of Gilead. It also borrows Pharaoh's chariots (Song 1-7).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Camphire in the vineyards of Engedi, the rose of Sharon, and a head like Carmel (Song 1:14; 2:1; 7:5).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Come with me from Lebanon; the tower of Lebanon looks toward Damascus (Song 4:8; 7:4).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: She is likened to a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots (Song 1:9).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Her eyes are like the fishpools in Heshbon, and her hair as a flock of goats from mount Gilead (Song 4:1; 7:4).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: The tower of Lebanon looketh toward Damascus, and the bride is called from the top of Shenir and Hermon (Song 4:8; 7:4).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country with a temple at any stage (as of October 2026) that was wholly or partly communist-ruled in the Cold War.
prompts.text_original: A country with a temple at any stage (dedicated, under construction or announced, as of October 2026) that, in whole or in part, had a communist government during the Cold War. Germany counts because Freiberg lay in East Germany.
prompts.summary: The Freiberg Germany Temple, dedicated in 1985, was the first temple built inside a communist state. Since then temples have been dedicated in Ukraine, Hong Kong and Cambodia, with others under construction in Hungary and Congo-Brazzaville and announced for Russia, Shanghai, Mongolia, Angola and Mozambique (as of October 2026).

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Freiberg Germany Temple (1985) was built in East Germany.

answers.name: Ukraine
answers.fact: Kyiv Ukraine Temple (2010); former Soviet republic.

answers.name: China
answers.fact: Shanghai temple announced; Hong Kong China Temple dedicated 1996.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: Budapest Hungary Temple under construction; Warsaw Pact state.

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: A temple in Russia is announced; former Soviet Union.

answers.name: Angola
answers.fact: Luanda Angola Temple announced (2023); People's Republic of Angola 1975-1992.

answers.name: Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: Brazzaville Republic of the Congo Temple under construction; People's Republic of the Congo 1969-1992.

answers.name: Cambodia
answers.fact: Phnom Penh Cambodia Temple (2026); communist governments 1975-1989.

answers.name: Mozambique
answers.fact: Beira and Maputo Mozambique temples announced; People's Republic of Mozambique 1975-1990.

answers.name: Mongolia
answers.fact: Ulaanbaatar Mongolia Temple announced; Soviet-aligned people's republic until 1990.

prompts.display_text: Pin an Asian country or territory where Church missionaries preached in the 1850s.
prompts.text_original: In 1852 the First Presidency called more than a hundred men to missions abroad, including India, Siam and China. Pin an Asian country or territory where Church missionaries went in the 1850s.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: India, Thailand, Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia; Newsroom facts and statistics: Sri Lanka; Saints vol. 2
prompts.summary: The 1852 mission calls sent elders across Asia. They reached Hong Kong and Ceylon in 1853, Singapore, Penang and Bangkok in 1854, and stations across British India, though few converts were made and the missions soon closed.

answers.name: India
answers.fact: Missionaries served in British India from the early 1850s, with sporadic missions from 1857 at Calcutta, Lahore and Srinagar.

answers.name: Hong Kong
answers.fact: Missionaries arrived in Hong Kong in April 1853.

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: Elam Luddington reached Bangkok, then the Kingdom of Siam, on April 6, 1854.

answers.name: Malaysia
answers.fact: Luddington preached in Penang and Malacca in 1854.

answers.name: Singapore
answers.fact: Luddington passed through Singapore in March 1854 on his way to Siam.

answers.name: Sri Lanka
answers.fact: Missionaries reached Ceylon, now Sri Lanka, in May 1853.

prompts.display_text: Pin an African country where the Church has between 20,000 and 50,000 members (end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: An African country where the Church had between 20,000 and 50,000 members at the end of 2025 (latest figures as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: Church facts and statistics country pages (31 Dec 2025)
prompts.summary: At the end of 2025 six African countries sat in the 20,000 to 50,000 member band: Sierra Leone (41,775), Mozambique (39,282), Uganda (26,304), Liberia (25,767), Kenya (24,547) and Madagascar (20,395). Zimbabwe (52,430) was just above the band, and Cabo Verde (16,334) just below.

answers.name: Kenya
answers.fact: 24,547 members, 2 missions.

answers.name: Sierra Leone
answers.fact: 41,775 members, 2 missions.

answers.name: Uganda
answers.fact: 26,304 members, 1 mission.

answers.name: Liberia
answers.fact: 25,767 members, 1 mission.

answers.name: Madagascar
answers.fact: 20,395 members, 2 missions.

answers.name: Mozambique
answers.fact: 39,282 members, 2 missions.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Latin American or Caribbean country or territory that got its first Church mission headquarters there between 1970 and 1989.
prompts.text_original: Between 1970 and 1989 the Church placed mission headquarters in many Latin American and Caribbean lands for the first time. Pin a Latin American or Caribbean country or territory that got its first Church mission headquartered there between 1970 and 1989.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Ecuador, Colombia, El Salvador, Paraguay, Puerto Rico, Dominican Republic, Honduras, Haiti, Barbados, Jamaica, Nicaragua, Panama
prompts.summary: From 1970 to 1989 the Church gave a first mission headquarters to Ecuador (1970), Colombia (1971), El Salvador (1976), Paraguay (1977), Puerto Rico (1979), the Dominican Republic and Honduras (1980), Barbados and Haiti (1984), Jamaica (1985), and Nicaragua and Panama (1989). Costa Rica is not an answer: it had hosted the Central American Mission headquarters since 1965.

answers.name: Dominican Republic
answers.fact: The Santo Domingo Dominican Republic Mission was organized January 1, 1980.

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: The Colombia Mission was created in Bogota in July 1971 from the Colombia-Venezuela Mission.

answers.name: Ecuador
answers.fact: The Ecuador Mission was organized in Quito in August 1970.

answers.name: Honduras
answers.fact: The Honduras Tegucigalpa Mission began operations February 4, 1980.

answers.name: Haiti
answers.fact: The Haiti Port-au-Prince Mission was organized August 4, 1984.

answers.name: Nicaragua
answers.fact: The Nicaragua Managua Mission was organized October 15, 1989.

answers.name: Panama
answers.fact: The Panama City Mission was created July 1, 1989.

answers.name: Paraguay
answers.fact: The Paraguay Asuncion Mission was created July 1, 1977.

answers.name: El Salvador
answers.fact: The El Salvador San Salvador Mission was organized July 1, 1976.

answers.name: Jamaica
answers.fact: The Jamaica Kingston Mission was organized July 1, 1985.

answers.name: Puerto Rico
answers.fact: The Puerto Rico San Juan Mission was created July 7, 1979.

answers.name: Barbados
answers.fact: Barbados became the headquarters of the West Indies Mission on June 26, 1984.
